nodes.label: Stats Must Be Retrievable Rule
nodes.rationale: Every displayed number must be retrievable from Postgres, a Zoho API, or a real social-platform API; curated constants (benchmarks, market CPM) only with EST · curated labels; no demographics, sentiment or real-time anywhere in Phase 1. Captured in Claude persistent memory as stats-must-be-retrievable.

nodes.label: Sponsor Portal Redesign Execution
nodes.rationale: All 4 sponsor pages rebuilt for client-demo wow: Command Deck hero + Executive Bento density with the radial gauge as ROI centerpiece; rich SVG + CSS motion, zero new deps, server-rendered; 28 provenance-chip usages; verified with tsc, next build, eslint, acceptance greps and a prod smoke test.

nodes.label: A2 State & Polish Execution (Portal-Wide Stats Wow)
nodes.rationale: 15 subagent-driven tasks: Frost light theme with pre-paint script, WCAG AA contrast pass, branded state system with ?demo= switcher on 13 pages, differentiated portal heroes (admin ops board, athlete milestone, property showcase), retrievable networkStats + CountUp replacing HERO_STATS, charts consolidation deleting line-chart.tsx. All build gates, acceptance greps and prod smoke tests passed.

nodes.label: SponsorX Zoho Field Mapping Document (P0-PMO-08)
nodes.rationale: v0.2: all nine §18 objects mapped field-by-field with direction and system-of-record per field, verified against the live iCARRe Foundation org metadata (103 field API names, 26 picklist values, 0 missing). Key findings: no external-ID field existed (gap G-1), Campaign maps to Deals not the stock Campaigns module, only 3 of 8 AthleteState values ever reach Zoho, nine Prisma schema gaps handed to P3-BE-01.

nodes.label: SponsorX_ID External Field on Five Zoho Modules (P0-OPS-06)
nodes.rationale: Closed gap G-1: SponsorX_ID text(50) external field created and verified on Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Deals, Tasks. Zoho lessons: uniqueness is case-insensitive only (never case-normalise ids), unique cannot combine with external (external is inherently unique), field labels cap at 25 chars and derive the api_name. Built in production because sandbox creation is UI-only and the OAuth token is production-scoped; a later sandbox inherits the work.

nodes.label: Content Partners Custom Zoho Module (P0-OPS-05)
nodes.rationale: Module shell was human click-work (Zoho CRM has no public create-module API — a permanent split), the eleven §6.2 fields were API work, all verified by metadata read-back. Organization module (not team) so sales staff can see records; default Email/record-image layout items stripped per §6.4. Mapper facts: Zoho prepends -None- to every picklist (omit rather than send), mandatory is a layout property unenforceable via API, removing a field from layout does not delete it.

nodes.label: Zoho Credentials & Sandbox Spec (P0-OPS-04)
nodes.rationale: OAuth scope list derived from the object register, not defaulted: no DELETE scope on any module and never ZohoCRM.modules.ALL, because the mapping suspends records and never deletes. Books scopes deferred until O-1 closes. Token rules: cache and refresh on expiry (Zoho caps refresh-token issuance), record who authorised (token dies with their account); domains are part of the data-residency answer (US DC).

nodes.label: Full Programme Task Board Build (All Four Phases)
nodes.rationale: Broke down Phases 2–4 from the detailed developer specifications into 343 (later 345) tasks / ~1,093 person-days / $350–535K across 7 xlsx sheets; renamed Phase-1-internal 'phases' to Stages; ID scheme P{stage}-{CAT}-{nn} for Phase 1, {phase}S{sprint}-{CAT}-{nn} for 2–4. Key risks recorded: Phase 2's ledger design precedes code, Phase 3 must never blend the four attribution meanings in a sponsor report.
